initial_answer:
No, the total formation-volume factor $ B_t $ is not simply the sum of $ B_o $ and $ B_g $, unless the pressure is above the bubble point pressure $ P_b $. Below $ P_b $, $ B_t $ accounts for the volume occupied by both the oil and the free gas that has come out of solution, and thus it is not just $ B_o + B_g $. The correct relationship is given by:

$$ B_t = B_o + B_g (R_{sb} - R_s) $$

This equation is derived from the definition of $ B_t $, which includes the volume of the gas that has evolved from the liquid [KB2]. Therefore, the total formation-volume factor $ B_t $ depends on the amount of gas that has come out of solution, and it is not always just $ B_o + B_g $.
